symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1810 (ako/mxcli#2129): under `run --local` with security on, Playwright probes that sign in once each and never sign out exhaust the unlicensed runtime's sessions; sign-ins 1-6 answer 200, the 7th and later HTTP 560 'Sign in failed', runtime log 'Maximum number of sessions exceeded! (You are currently using a trial license)'. mxcli had no way to free them short of stopping the app and deleting from "system$session" by hand.
cause: The trial licence caps concurrent sessions at 6 and counts the System.Session rows in the database. Each sign-in holds a row until sign-out or expiry; a probe loop fills them in seconds. Nothing in `mxcli run` deleted them.
file: cmd/mxcli/cmd_run_sessions.go (run clear-sessions, runDatabaseFromArgs), cmd/mxcli/docker/sessions_clear.go (ClearSessions, clearSessionRows), cmd/mxcli/docker/runlocal.go (RunDatabase), cmd/mxcli/docker/screenshot_login.go (hint names the command)
insight: Measure before building on the report's theory. The first fix cleared System.Session at boot, on the report's claim that rows outlive a restart (20 had piled up). On 11.12.1 the rows do survive a graceful stop (6 left), but the runtime logs 'Deleting old sessions from database...' as it starts and boots with 0, so the boot clear was redundant and the old hint's 'restart clears them' was right. The question that mattered was whether the cap is counted in memory or in the table: deleting the rows from a LIVE app made the next sign-in succeed, so a no-restart command is possible. Run it end to end with curl against /xas/ login (no browser needed: each curl without a cookie jar is a fresh session): 6x200, 560, control 560 without clearing, clear-sessions, 6x200. The real schema also has FKs (session_user ON DELETE CASCADE, backgroundjob/changehash SET NULL), so a plain delete is safe. Infra trap: a Postgres data dir under the 0700 session scratchpad PANICs mid-test when the tree's perms are tightened; put it in /var/tmp.
